purpose: Guides imaging work-up of an adrenal incidentaloma on CT or MRI, an adrenal mass found on imaging done for reasons other than suspected adrenal disease, to decide whether it is benign.
system: ESE-ENSAT clinical practice guideline on the management of adrenal incidentalomas (2023): imaging work-up
aliases: european society of endocrinology adrenal incidentaloma

inputs.label: History of extra-adrenal malignancy
inputs.how_stated: true when the clinical details or dictation state a current or previous cancer outside the adrenal (e.g. staging or follow-up CT for lung cancer); false when no cancer history is given and the scan is for another reason; a lesion only suspected of being cancer ("suspicious for", "possible", "cannot be excluded"), here or elsewhere, is not a known cancer

locator.section: 2.1 Definition: masses found at staging or follow-up of extra-adrenal malignancy do not meet the strict definition; addressed in 5.6.3

inputs.label: Imaging for suspected adrenal disease or hereditary-syndrome screening
inputs.how_stated: true when the scan was done to investigate suspected adrenal disease (e.g. signs or symptoms of phaeochromocytoma, Cushing's or Conn's syndrome), or as screening in a hereditary syndrome that predisposes to adrenal tumours; false when the mass is incidental on a scan done for something else

locator.section: 2.1 Definition: imaging not performed for suspected adrenal disease; screening in hereditary syndromes falls outside the definition

inputs.label: Adrenal mass maximum diameter
inputs.how_stated: maximum diameter of the adrenal mass in centimetres (millimetres convert), e.g. '2.4 cm left adrenal nodule' or '24 x 18 mm'

locator.table: Figure 5: tumor < 4 cm / >= 4 cm; 2.1 p4: work-up threshold 1 cm

inputs.label: Appearance of the mass
inputs.how_stated: homogeneous: uniform density or signal throughout. heterogeneous: not uniform. clearly_benign: only when the dictation makes a specific benign diagnosis from imaging features other than attenuation, e.g. a myelolipoma with macroscopic fat; 'probable adenoma' is not enough

locator.table: Table 4 note a: homogeneous = uniform density or signal intensity throughout; masses with other clear benign characteristics, e.g. myelolipoma

inputs.label: Attenuation on unenhanced CT
inputs.how_stated: mean attenuation of the mass on unenhanced (noncontrast) CT in Hounsfield units, e.g. '8 HU on the unenhanced phase' or 'precontrast density 25 HU'. not_assessable when there is no unenhanced CT (contrast-enhanced phases only, or MRI only); enhanced-phase values do not count

inputs.label: Age
inputs.how_stated: patient's age in years from the clinical details or dictation, e.g. '34-year-old'

outcomes.classification: Adrenal nodule under 1 cm: below ESE's 1 cm threshold for incidentaloma work-up.
outcomes.recommendation: Further adrenal work-up is not routinely needed unless there are clinical signs or symptoms of adrenal hormone excess.
caveats: ESE calls the 1 cm work-up threshold arbitrary; it applies the threshold to further diagnostic work-up in general, imaging and hormonal.
Routing every sub-centimetre nodule here whatever its appearance or attenuation is the library's reading of section 2.1.

locator.section: 2.1 Definition, etiology and epidemiology: work-up threshold of 1 cm

outcomes.classification: Homogeneous adrenal mass of 10 HU or less on unenhanced CT: consistent with a benign (lipid-rich) lesion, whatever its size.
caveats: Clinical and hormonal assessment is still recommended: 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test, and aldosterone/renin ratio if there is hypertension or unexplained hypokalaemia.
Metanephrines are needed only when unenhanced attenuation is over 10 HU.
Surgery is not recommended for an asymptomatic, non-functioning unilateral mass with obvious benign imaging features.
In very young patients ESE would consider one follow-up scan at 12 months even for a presumably benign mass.
Under 40 years (or in pregnancy), ESE recommends urgent assessment of any adrenal mass.

locator.section: 5.2 R.2.3; Figure 5 p18; R.3.2, R.3.10 p2-3; Figure 4 note 3 p17; R.4.2 p24; 5.6.2 reasoning p30; R.6.2.1 p30

outcomes.classification: Adrenal mass with clear benign imaging features other than attenuation (e.g. myelolipoma).
outcomes.recommendation: No further imaging during follow-up is recommended for a lesion with clear benign imaging features.
caveats: ESE's imaging criteria apply to homogeneous masses or masses with other clear benign characteristics, such as myelolipoma; Figure 4 sends a non-functioning benign lesion (e.g. myelolipoma) to no further investigation. Requiring a firm imaging diagnosis for this route is a library addition.
Clinical and hormonal assessment is still recommended for every incidentaloma (1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test).
After MDT discussion, surgery may be considered for mass effect, e.g. a large myelolipoma that keeps growing.
Under 40 years (or in pregnancy), ESE recommends urgent assessment of any adrenal mass.

locator.section: 5.5 R.5.1; Figure 4 p17; Table 4 note a p19; R.3.1, R.3.2 p2; R.4.2 reasoning p24; R.6.2.1 p30

outcomes.classification: Homogeneous adrenal mass of 1 cm or more, not characterised: no unenhanced CT attenuation available.
outcomes.recommendation: Unenhanced (noncontrast) CT is recommended to establish whether the mass is homogeneous and lipid-rich, and therefore benign.
caveats: Standard contrast-enhanced CT is usually not helpful to tell benign from malignant adrenal masses.
MRI rather than CT is suggested in children, adolescents and pregnant women; if chemical-shift MRI has already been done and is unambiguous, an expert MDT may judge it sufficient.
Clinical and hormonal assessment is recommended for every incidentaloma (1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test).
Under 40 years (or in pregnancy), ESE recommends urgent assessment of any adrenal mass.

outcomes.classification: Homogeneous adrenal mass under 4 cm, 11-20 HU on unenhanced CT: indeterminate, low likelihood of malignancy.
outcomes.recommendation: Suggest immediate additional imaging (FDG-PET/CT, chemical-shift MRI or washout CT); alternatively, noncontrast CT or MRI in 12 months.
caveats: Applies when the hormonal work-up shows no significant hormone excess; it includes plasma or urinary metanephrines because attenuation is over 10 HU.
If the additional imaging suggests a benign lesion, no further imaging is required. Which test depends on local expertise and availability.
ESE recommends MDT discussion when imaging is not consistent with a benign lesion.
Pregnancy: ESE recommends urgent assessment, suggests MRI rather than CT, and suggests surgical resection if the mass is indeterminate on imaging.

locator.section: 5.2 R.2.4 and reasoning; Figure 5 and note 1 p18; R.3.9 p24; R.1.1 p16; R.6.2.1-6.2.3 p30

outcomes.classification: Indeterminate adrenal mass: homogeneous 11-20 HU and 4 cm or more, homogeneous over 20 HU and under 4 cm, or heterogeneous and under 4 cm.
outcomes.recommendation: Suggest MDT discussion; immediate additional imaging is usually preferred (or immediate surgery). If still indeterminate and not operated, ESE recommends noncontrast CT or MRI in 6-12 months.
caveats: ESE judges the likelihood of malignancy in this group still low, but higher than in masses under 4 cm of 11-20 HU.
With bilateral lesions of similar imaging features, biopsy could be considered.
Exclude phaeochromocytoma with plasma or urinary metanephrines.
On follow-up, surgical resection is suggested if the mass grows by more than 20% in maximum diameter and by at least 5 mm.
Pregnancy: ESE recommends urgent assessment, suggests MRI rather than CT, and suggests surgical resection if the mass is indeterminate on imaging.

locator.section: 5.2 R.2.6 and reasoning; Figure 5 and note 2 p18; R.3.9 p24; R.5.2 p26; R.6.2.1-6.2.3 p30

outcomes.classification: Adrenal mass 4 cm or more that is heterogeneous or over 20 HU on unenhanced CT: relevant risk of malignancy.
outcomes.recommendation: Suggest MDT discussion; usually surgery after complete staging (at least thoracic CT and/or FDG-PET/CT); additional imaging is an option in some patients.
caveats: If surgery is not performed, follow-up imaging (noncontrast CT or MRI) in 6-12 months is recommended.
When a mass meets both the size and the attenuation or heterogeneity criteria, malignancy may be as likely as 50%.
Exclude phaeochromocytoma with metanephrines; sex steroids and steroid precursors are suggested when adrenocortical carcinoma is suspected.
ESE recommends urgent assessment in pregnancy and under 40 years.
The figure places this group above 4 cm; the recommendation text (4 cm or more) is followed at exactly 4 cm.

locator.section: 5.2 R.2.5 and reasoning; Figure 5 and note 3 p18; R.3.9 p24; R.2.8 p20; R.6.2.1 p30; Figure 4 note 2 p17

outcomes.classification: Indeterminate adrenal mass in a patient under 40: higher likelihood of malignancy and of clinically significant hormone excess.
outcomes.recommendation: Urgent assessment is recommended; ESE suggests surgical resection if the mass is indeterminate on imaging.
caveats: Time-consuming diagnostic procedures should be avoided, and surgery, if indicated, should not be significantly delayed.
MRI rather than CT is suggested in children and adolescents if dedicated adrenal imaging is required.
ESE recommends MDT discussion when imaging is not consistent with a benign lesion; exclude phaeochromocytoma with metanephrines.

outcomes.classification: Known extra-adrenal malignancy, imaging for suspected adrenal disease, or hereditary-syndrome screening: outside ESE's incidentaloma pathway (Figure 5); with known malignancy, ESE's Figure 9 pathway applies.
outcomes.recommendation: Manage per the clinical context (library addition).
caveats: Known extra-adrenal malignancy: in principle the same ESE recommendations apply, through its separate pathway (Figure 9); always take life expectancy into account.
ESE recommends no further specific adrenal imaging follow-up for a lesion characterised as benign on noncontrast CT; with relevant hormone excess, treatment is individualised.
Strong FDG uptake on PET-CT suggests metastasis; with moderate or no uptake, ESE recommends further work-up with at least unenhanced CT.

Indeterminate lesion: ESE recommends excluding phaeochromocytoma. If proving malignancy would change management, it suggests FDG-PET/CT, resection or biopsy; otherwise it recommends imaging follow-up at the primary malignancy's interval.

locator.section: 5.6.3 general remarks and R.6.3.1-6.3.4 pp30-32; Figure 9 and notes 1-2 p31; 2.1 Definition p4

summary.text: Every adrenal incidentaloma needs dedicated imaging to decide whether it is homogeneous and lipid-rich, and therefore benign; noncontrast CT is the first-line test.
Homogeneous masses of 10 HU or less on unenhanced CT are benign and need no further imaging, whatever their size. All other masses should be discussed in an expert MDT.

locator.section: Abstract, selected recommendation 1

summary.text: Every patient needs clinical and hormonal work-up: 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test (cortisol 50 nmol/L or less excludes autonomous secretion), metanephrines when not typical of adenoma, and aldosterone/renin ratio with hypertension or hypokalaemia.

locator.section: Summary of recommendations R.3.1-3.3, R.3.9, R.3.10

summary.text: Indeterminate masses not operated on: one repeat noncontrast CT or MRI in 6-12 months; resection suggested for growth over 20% in maximum diameter and at least 5 mm.

definitions.text: Adrenal incidentaloma: an adrenal mass found on imaging not done for suspected adrenal disease. Masses found on hereditary-syndrome screening or cancer staging fall outside the strict definition; work-up applies from 1 cm.

locator.section: 2.1 Definition, etiology and epidemiology

definitions.text: Homogeneous mass: uniform density or signal intensity throughout. The region of interest should cover at least 75% of the lesion without contamination from tissue outside it.
Relative washout = 100 x (HUmax - HU10/15min) / HUmax; absolute washout = 100 x (HUmax - HU10/15min) / (HUmax - HUunenhanced), from unenhanced, 60-second and 10 or 15 minute delayed phases.

pitfalls.text: Not for adrenal masses found at staging or follow-up of a known extra-adrenal malignancy (ESE's separate pathway, Figure 9), on imaging for suspected adrenal disease, or on hereditary-syndrome screening.

locator.section: 2.1 Definition

pitfalls.text: ESE recommends against adrenal biopsy in the work-up of adrenal masses unless there is a history of extra-adrenal malignancy and its three criteria are met.
Heterogeneous masses should not go on to MRI or washout CT for characterisation; Table 4 criteria apply only to homogeneous masses or clear benign entities such as myelolipoma.
The 58% relative washout cut-off rests on a single study of 253 tumours and should be used with caution; older studies suggest 40%.
With bilateral or multiple adrenal masses, assess each lesion separately by the same imaging protocol; review the contralateral adrenal, which is often also hyperplastic or nodular.
Some metastases (e.g. from kidney cancer or low-grade lymphoma) may be FDG-negative, and some benign tumours (e.g. functioning adenomas) are FDG-positive.
